title: Shipwright intent.md (parsed shape)
description: The parsed shape of .shipwright/planning/intent.md, the human-owned top of the intent pyramid. File format: YAML front matter with `intent_version: 1` and `product`, then four `##` sections in this order: Intent, Non-goals, Capabilities, Key scenarios. Each element is one line `- <ID>: <text> [<status>]`, a capability `- CAP-nn <name>: <text> [<status>]` (the short name used in reports); the status is always last, never in front of the text (ID INT-nn, NG-nn, CAP-nn, SCN-nn; status confirmed or assumption). The file holds human text only: no FR ids (every link to an FR lives on the AI side). There are deliberately NO upper limits on counts or text length (operator 2026-11-28); size is information in a report, never a rule. Counts and cross-element rules (each CAP has a scenario, each FR one CAP) belong to gate P (U1b), not to this schema. Ids are never reused once an element has been confirmed (an FR link to a removed id is a gate-P finding, U1b). Rewording a confirmed element needs a change-flow record, otherwise F11 refuses it; the confirmation evidence (id plus text hash) lives outside intent.md (U2a1). Every non-blank line under the four sections must parse as an element (an unparseable line is an error, never silently dropped), ids are unique per file and zero-padding is part of the id (both U1b rules; the schema cannot express them). A missing file means no intent declared. One file per repository for now. The parser arrives in U1b; this schema fixes the shape it produces.

text.description: Human text on one line, trimmed, no FR id and no id of another element (links live on the AI side). No maximum length.
